diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$ be a bounded polyhedral Lipschitz domain.
Furthermore, we use the Sobolev embedding $V\hookrightarrow L^p(\Omega)$ with $p\in[2,\infty)$ if $d=2$ and $p\in[2,6]$ if $d=3$.
Therefore, the $u$-dependent diffusion model \eqref{eq:quasi-u-diffusion} satisfies (C3) on $B_{\rho}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The (C3) derivation for u-dependent diffusion bounds the bilinear terms through L^∞ controls: ||a(·,w)-a(·,z)||_∞ ≤ K₁(ρ)C_∞||w-z||_V (eq:quasi-u-coeffdiff), ||∂_s a(·,w)-∂_s a(·,z)||_∞ ≤ K₂(ρ)C_∞||w-z||_V, and ||δu||_∞ ≤ C_∞||δu||_V (eq:quasi-u-term2). But in the paper's own setting V = H¹₀(Ω) with d ∈ {2,3} (Section 2.1), the embedding H¹₀(Ω) ↪ L^∞(Ω) fails — H¹₀ contains unbounded functions — so no finite C_∞ exists; the ball B_ρ likewise contains unbounded functions, so M_∞(ρ) does not exist. The paper itself restricts the available embeddings to V ↪ L^p with p < ∞ (Section 2.3). Hence the stated hypothesis is unsatisfiable and the closing claim that the model satisfies (C3) on B_ρ is unsupported as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the two term bounds with the available H¹₀ ↪ L^p embeddings (p ≤ 6 for d=3) and Hölder exponents, e.g. ||a(·,w)-a(·,z)||_{L^p} ≤ K₁(ρ)C_p||w-z||_V and ||δu||_{L^{p'}} ≤ C_{p'}||δu||_V, replacing every L^∞ control; this yields a larger but valid computable L(ρ) and restores (C3) for the model without changing the NK framework.
issues.overall_effect: The representative quasilinear (C3) certification (eq:quasi-u-C3 with the computable L(ρ) in eq:quasi-u-Lrho) is not established in the paper's function space; the advertised quasilinear Lipschitz ingredient is invalid as stated. The abstract NK theorem (thm:NK) and the semilinear (C3) bounds are unaffected.
issues.title: Quasilinear (C3) example relies on an impossible H^1_0 ↪ L^∞ embedding assumption
issues.why_classification: Repair needs a contained but nontrivial re-derivation of the example's estimates (new Hölder splittings and constants), and the specific L(ρ) formula advertised is withdrawn; however no main theorem depends on this illustrative example, so the loss is limited to the quasilinear (C3) route — a moderate, not serious, loss.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition 8.1 gives width_base = L_{J₂}(ρ)ρ with L_{J₂}(ρ) = C₂(||ũ_h||₂ + C₂ρ), the bound stated in the remark after subsec:qoi:examples and invoked in subsec:numerics:qoi-baseline. The linear-QoI row of tab:sec9-qoi-linear (width_base = C₂ρ since ||ψ||₂ = 1) pins C₂ = 0.1599427/0.71060674 = 0.2250791 = 1/(π√2). With ||ũ_h||₂ = √(2×0.12280009514167282) = 0.4955806 and ρ = 0.71060674001423230 (tab:sec9-cert), the stated formula gives 0.2250791×(0.4955806+0.1599428)×0.71060674 = 0.1048462, but tab:sec9-qoi-quadratic reports 1.176370e-01. The reported value instead equals C₂||ũ_h||₂ρ + (3/2)C₂²ρ² = 0.0792645 + 0.0383725 = 0.1176370, and this same alternative formula reproduces all five reported QoI2 widths to about 8 significant digits. Thus the table was computed with an unstated extra ½C₂²ρ² term and does not match the paper's claim that Proposition 8.1 yields the reported widths. (The reported width exceeds the valid Proposition 8.1 bound, so the enclosure itself remains valid.)

failure_location.quote: We report the certified intervals and their widths, see Table \ref{tab:sec9-qoi-linear}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the width_base column as L_{J₂}(ρ)ρ = C₂(||ũ_h||₂ + C₂ρ)ρ (≈ 0.10485 for N=16), or explicitly state the alternative bound (Proposition 8.1 width plus a ½M_{J₂}ρ² Taylor-remainder term) actually used.
issues.overall_effect: The reported baseline enclosures for the quadratic QoI cannot be reproduced from the paper's stated formula and constants; the prose 'Proposition 8.1 yields …' is inaccurate for QoI2. No theorem is invalidated and the reported intervals remain valid enclosures.
issues.title: Baseline width for the quadratic QoI is inconsistent with the stated Proposition 8.1 formula
issues.why_classification: A local numerical correction or one-sentence clarification restores consistency; every certified guarantee survives because the reported interval is still valid (it is wider than the Proposition 8.1 bound), and no proof, rate, or advertised scope is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\mathsf{Adm}(\rho)\ \text{holds for all }\rho\in[\rho_{\rm low},\rho_*),
\quad
\mathsf{Adm}(\rho)\ \text{fails for all }\rho\in[\rho_*,\rho_{\rm up}],

issues.failure_explanation: The proof correctly derives that {ρ>0 : p(ρ) ≤ 0} = [ρ₋,ρ₊] is a closed interval (p strictly convex), but then asserts AD = [ρ₋,min{ρ₊,ρ_q}) and that this 'is of the claimed form [ρ₋,ρ₊)'. When the p-constraint binds strictly inside the q-region, i.e. p(ρ₊)=0 with q(ρ₊)<1, the endpoint ρ₊ belongs to AD, so AD = [ρ₋,ρ₊] is closed, not [ρ₋,ρ₊); the threshold claim 'Adm fails for all ρ ∈ [ρ_*,ρ_up]' then fails at ρ_* = ρ₊. Counterexample within the lemma's hypotheses: α=1, 𝔯 = 5/16 (so η = 5/16), L(ρ) = 1+ρ; then p(ρ) = 5/16 + (ρ²+ρ³)/2 − ρ vanishes at ρ = 1/2 and at ρ = (√29−3)/4 ≈ 0.5962, and q((√29−3)/4) ≈ 0.9517 < 1, so AD = [1/2, (√29−3)/4] is closed while the lemma claims the half-open form.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Amend the lemma to state that AD is empty or a closed or half-open interval [ρ₋,ρ₊] or [ρ₋,ρ₊) with ρ₊ = sup AD, and change the threshold claim to 'Adm fails for all ρ ∈ (ρ_*,ρ_up]'; no change to the algorithm or its guarantees is needed.
issues.overall_effect: Only the endpoint form of AD and the strict threshold statement of Lemma lem:adm-interval are false as written. The interval structure (AD is an interval) survives, and the correctness of Algorithm alg:rho (Proposition prop:alg-rho-correct) is unaffected because bisection works identically whether or not the right endpoint is attained.
issues.title: Lemma lem:adm-interval: admissible set can be closed on the right, contradicting the claimed [ρ₋,ρ₊) form
issues.why_classification: A one-line statement correction repairs the defect with no new argument and no loss; the interval structure, the bisection correctness, and all numerical conclusions survive unchanged.
